fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Three Ages of Stone Stacked on Top of Each Other", "body": "Camille Sauvé builds much of her book Sorcerers of Stone on the work of a Cuscanian researcher named Alfredo Gamara, who identified three distinct construction styles in Peru and called them Hananpacha, Uranpacha and Ukupacha. Her central visual argument is over building: an older style sits underneath the megalithic work, and the far more recent Inca, Kilke and Ware masonry sits on top of and around both, often fitted into the grooves and recesses of the oldest layer. Sauvé argues that later cultures recognized this earlier work as sacred and deliberately built into it rather than replacing it."}, {"title": "The Hananpacha Layer Nobody Talks About", "body": "Sauvé says the megalithic walls get all the attention while the stranger, older Hananpacha work goes largely unstudied. These are gray metamorphosed limestone forms that read as art projects rather than buildings: stepped chicanas, carved basins, surreal shapes with no windows, doorways or ceilings and no obvious use as shelter. She reports finding the same forms far outside Peru, in Japan, Bulgaria, Germany, beneath the Egyptian pyramids, and in the foundation stone under the Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem, where both Jewish and Muslim tradition place the creation of the earth. That global spread, she contends, points toward a single worldwide civilization."}, {"title": "Seke Lines, Charged Rock and Doorways to Elsewhere", "body": "Sauvé describes 42 seke lines radiating out from the Coricancha sun temple in Cusco, with the huacas, or sacred sites, placed directly along them. She suggests these lines follow fracture zones and underground water passages, creating discontinuity zones where telluric currents flow and where quartz rich rock can hold electromagnetic charge. Andean pacos and shamans still come to these places to pray to the Apus and Pachamama and, she believes, to enter altered states. She recounts Jim Wills reportedly opening a portal at Aramu Muru near Lake Titicaca by chanting three tones, and local legends of people vanishing while singing at these doorways."}, {"title": "Expanding Earth, Pangaea and the Global Flood Record", "body": "Garton and Sauvé chase the possibility that the earth itself has grown. Sauvé notes that Nikola Tesla, Newton and Darwin all entertained expansion, with Darwin reading stepped coastal layers in Patagonia as evidence and Tesla describing a condensation of etheric material swelling every celestial body. She cites Ben Noel of the Ben Franklin Theoretical Research Institute of Australia proposing 200 million years, while stressing that none of this is concrete truth. Alongside it she stacks roughly 300 worldwide flood legends, the Aymara language's reported kinship with Japanese, and a proto Sumerian inscribed bowl unearthed near Tiwanaku."}, {"title": "Geopolymers Versus the Quarry and Copper Chisel Story", "body": "The strongest thread is Sauvé's case that these stones were poured, not carved. She points to scoop marks about four inches wide, pressed in fingerprint like impressions in the living rock, and vitrification that would require roughly 1400 Celsius. She recounts Russian geologists invited by Peru's Ministry of Culture in 2012 who tested about 30 samples, found a microcrystalline structure with the fossils pulverized out, and concluded geopolymer, an answer the Ministry disliked. Garton reads Garcilaso de la Vega's account of 20,000 men hauling one boulder that fell and crushed more than 3,000, and calls the quarrying story comical."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Author and ancient civilization investigator Camille Sauvé joins InnerVerse to discuss her book, Sorcerers of Stone: Architects of the Three Ages. While investigating the hundreds of other-worldly structures around Peru, Camille discovered unsolved mysteries that connect unexplained megalithic sites worldwide. Tune in for topics including leylines, altered states, portals, cataclysms, expanding Earth theories, geopolymer technologies, and a show & tell of epic "Cyclopean" masonry in Peru.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: In the Plus+ Extension we look at sites worldwide that resemble the Peruvian architecture, consider evidence for giant petrified animals, ask whether ancient sites were engineered for acoustic resonance and sound healing, learn of psychic activations and metaphysical initiations, free energy and antiquitech potentials, applied Biogeometry, dowsing, and mysterious hybrid human mummies of Nazca.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "A World Tour of Matching Stonework", "body": "Once Camille moves past Peru, she walks through a photographic tour of matching stonework in Japan, China, Italy and Jerusalem, including the Beau Marzo pyramid and the foundation stone beneath the Dome of the Rock. The same odd knobs, niches, basins and fingerprint like impressions show up everywhere, even where the mainstream explanation of rope and lifting boss makes no sense, since some knobs angle upward with nothing above them to lift. She argues these traits point to one shared building tradition or technology spanning continents, not isolated cultures independently inventing identical, impractical decorative marks."}, {"title": "Sound, Resonance and Sacred Chambers", "body": "Camille describes the resonance chambers cut into Peru's rock, including the ten niches at Naupa Iglesia where guides test tones until one hits resonance and echoes across the whole valley, and a similar harmonic chamber at Machu Picchu. As a professional biofield tuner himself, Chance connects this to sound healing, and Camille describes shamans chanting into the niches for altered states and priests possibly using them for ritual healing. She notes quartz and calcite in the rock may amplify these frequencies, turning entire outcrops into natural sound chambers built for ceremony rather than shelter."}, {"title": "Earth Energy, Water Memory and Dowsing", "body": "Camille lays out her theory that these sites sit on fracture zones and underground water sources that generate teleric currents, with quartz rich stone storing electromagnetic energy that visitors can feel as vibration or even personal energy events. Chance recounts using dowsing rods professionally in remote biofield tuning sessions and describes a friend naming unfamiliar mountains that his rods located correctly, arguing this taps a shared subconscious or quantum field rather than trickery. Camille frames water itself as a possible memory carrier, moving between wakas and linking sacred sites into one living communication network."}, {"title": "Mercury, Light and Lost Technologies", "body": "Prompted by reports of liquid mercury pools beneath pyramids at Teotihuacan, the conversation turns to mercury's alchemical reputation and its strange physical behavior, including how magnetized mercury spins and can generate light without flame, which might explain windowless tombs and pyramid chambers that show no scorch marks. Camille connects this to bio geometry research using pendulums to test how shapes and forms hold energy patterns, and to her hope that subtle energy researchers with proper instruments will eventually study Peru's wakas the way they already study similar sites in Egypt, France and Germany."}, {"title": "Nasca Mummies and the Deeper Mystery", "body": "Camille brings up the Nasca mummies with elongated skulls, noting genetic testing has reportedly found human DNA mixed with unknown and even chimpanzee derived sequences among the roughly fifteen bodies recovered so far, some dated to only fifteen hundred years ago. She pairs this with Chuah oral history about goblin like DW beings said to emerge from the mountains at dawn, wondering whether hybrid beings or hidden subterranean life could explain the region's stranger stonework. She closes the exclusive material by recommending David Childress, Freddie Silva and Rudolf Steiner's Cosmic Memory as further reading for listeners who want to go deeper."}]
